key_insight: FAMOS can infer object articulation from a sparse, unordered set of partial 3D observations instead of relying on a single view. By combining evidence across multiple incomplete point clouds, it predicts both movable-part segmentation and joint parameters more robustly.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the difficulty of modeling articulated objects from sparse monocular views, where each observation reveals only partial geometry and motion cues. Existing feed-forward approaches often depend on strong category-level priors because they infer articulation from only one observation.
method: Takes a sparse, unordered set of partial point clouds as input rather than a single image or view.
Jointly reasons over multiple observations to estimate movable-part segmentation and joint parameters.
Uses a feed-forward design to directly predict articulation structure without requiring slow iterative optimization at inference time.
impact: This matters because it makes articulated-object understanding more practical in real-world sparse-view settings, such as robotics and 3D perception. For practitioners, it offers a way to infer motion structure more reliably from incomplete data and with less dependence on category-specific assumptions.

paper_title: FAMOS: Feed-Forward 3D Articulation Modeling from Sparse Observations
paper_authors: Kevin Qu, Tao Sun, Massimiliano Viola, Liyuan Zhu, Zhizhuo Zhou
